Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Banking and Finance Secondary market turnover surges by 152% to GH¢6.86bn Source : Joy Business 18 November 2026 5:20pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The secondary market turnover surged by 152.49% week-on-week to GH¢6.86 billion.
Trading activity shifted towards the 2031-2034 maturity segment, which dominated turnover with a 49.70% share at a weighted-average yield of 14.97%.
The 2027-2030 segment followed closely, accounting for 47.97% of turnover at a weighted-average yield of 12.92%.
The post-2035 maturities attracted a modest 2.33% share at a weighted-average yield of 14.92%.
“ We expect secondary market activity to remain tactical this week as investors position ahead of the February 2027 DDEP [Domestic Debt Exchange Programme]” bond buyback,” said Databank Research. The exercise will be conducted through a Dutch auction scheduled for 23 rd – 25 th November 2026, with settlement on 26 November 2026.
“However, we believe the market-based pricing, capped at par value, could limit participation as bondholders weigh immediate liquidity against potential capital losses and foregone coupon income. Meanwhile, we anticipate the Bank of Ghana will maintain its policy rate at 14.00% on 18 Nov’26, reinforcing near-term interest rate stability”.
